summary.title: Xiaomi OneVL: One-Step Latent Reasoning and Planning with Vision-Language Explanation

setting_and_object.category: Algorithm (VLA framework / latent chain-of-thought with world-model supervision)

details: Explicit autoregressive CoT improves driving trajectory prediction but its token-by-token generation makes latency prohibitive for real-time deployment.

Prior latent CoT methods (COCONUT, CODI, SIM-CoT) compress only linguistic reasoning — a symbolic abstraction rather than the causal scene dynamics — and consistently underperform explicit CoT, while still generating latents sequentially.
OneVL: a VLA framework where reasoning is routed through a small fixed set of visual and language latent tokens inserted before the trajectory answer.

Crux: dual training-only auxiliary decoders supervise these latents — a language decoder reconstructing the text CoT, and a visual 'world model' decoder that predicts discrete visual tokens of near-future frames, forcing the bottleneck to encode causal scene dynamics.

At inference the decoders are dropped and all latent tokens are prefilled into the prompt in one parallel pass, giving answer-only latency; a three-stage curriculum (main-model warmup, frozen-backbone decoder warmup, joint fine-tuning) makes joint optimization stable.
Backbone Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (ViT + MLP aligner + LLM); auxiliary decoders are additional 4B-scale instances (≈3x training memory, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2).
4 visual latent tokens and 2 language latent tokens (realized as 35 and 20 existing-vocabulary tokens; adding new special tokens degraded performance), delimited by start/end markers.

Both decoders receive current-frame ViT patch embeddings concatenated with MLP-projected latent hidden states; visual targets are IBQ/Emu3.5 discrete tokens (131,072-code vocabulary, 512x512 images) for frames at +0.5s and +1.0s.
Preliminary self-supervised pretraining of the visual decoder as an unconditional future-frame generator (13,040 steps, batch 256, lr 1e-4).
Stage 0: full VLM trained on trajectory prediction with latent tokens embedded (2 epochs, lr 4e-5, batch 64).
Stage 1: main VLM frozen, both auxiliary decoders trained (1 epoch, lr 1e-4).
Stage 2: joint end-to-end fine-tuning of all components (5 epochs, lr 1e-4), turning the visual decoder into an action-conditioned world model.
NAVSIM (PDM score), ROADWork (ADE/FDE), Impromptu (ADE/FDE and 1–4s L2), Alpamayo-R1 (ADE/FDE); inference latency reported everywhere.

CoT supervision: AdaThinkDrive-released traces on NAVSIM; in-house work-zone pipeline on ROADWork; decision/root-cause labels built from Q&A on Impromptu; Chain-of-Causation labels regenerated with the released Alpamayo-R1 10B checkpoint (waypoints subsampled 64→8; 700-clip self-built test set).
Same-backbone baselines: AR Answer-only, AR CoT+Answer, and adapted COCONUT, CODI, SIM-CoT (6 epochs, lr 4e-5, batch 64).
Published SOTA references: AdaThinkDrive (8B), LaST-VLA (8B) on NAVSIM; YNet on ROADWork; Impromptu VLA; Cosmos-Reason (10B) on Alpamayo-R1.
Ablations: remove visual decoder, remove language decoder, remove three-stage curriculum (direct joint training); deployment variant with an MLP trajectory head on the last latent hidden state.
Text CoT quality on 500 NAVSIM test samples via meta-action exact-match, BGE-reranker-v2-m3 semantic similarity, and Gemini LLM-as-judge (0–100 across perception, motion state, decision, fluency).

key_findings.finding: OneVL is the first latent CoT method to beat explicit autoregressive CoT while running at answer-only latency.
key_findings.evidence: NAVSIM: 88.84 PDM vs 88.29 for AR CoT+Answer, 87.47 for AR Answer, 87.30 LaST-VLA (8B) and 86.20 AdaThinkDrive (8B); latency 4.46s vs 4.49s for AR Answer and ~1.5x faster than explicit CoT. ROADWork 12.49 ADE / 28.80 FDE vs YNet 22.68/80.78 (2.3x faster than explicit CoT); Impromptu avg L2 1.01 vs 1.22 for Impromptu VLA; Alpamayo-R1 ADE 2.62 (best) with FDE 7.53 vs Cosmos-Reason 10B's 2.86/7.42.

key_findings.finding: Existing language-only latent CoT methods fail to transfer to VLA driving, generally falling below even answer-only prediction.
key_findings.evidence: Adapted COCONUT, CODI and SIM-CoT underperform AR Answer across benchmarks (e.g., on Alpamayo-R1: 3.29/3.22/3.40 ADE vs 3.27 for AR Answer and 2.99 for AR CoT), and their sequential latent generation is even slower (3.76–3.85s vs 3.06s).

key_findings.finding: The visual world-model decoder is the larger source of gain, exceeding the language decoder's contribution.
key_findings.evidence: NAVSIM ablation: removing the visual decoder drops PDM from 88.84 to 87.97 (-0.87), while removing the language decoder drops it to 88.53 (-0.31).

key_findings.finding: The three-stage curriculum is essential; direct joint end-to-end training collapses into memorization.
key_findings.evidence: PDM falls from 88.84 to 67.13 without staging; initial gradient norm explodes to 378.22 vs 0.28 with staging, final trajectory loss is worse (0.186 vs 0.136), and decoded 'future' frames become artifacts unrelated to the input image with erroneous language CoT.

key_findings.finding: Compressed latents retain decodable, reasonably faithful language explanations and support a very low-latency deployment variant.
key_findings.evidence: Language decoder reaches 71.00 meta-action accuracy (vs 67.20 for SIM-CoT), 78.26 STS and 79.13 LLM-judge, approaching the AR CoT upper bound; an MLP trajectory head yields 86.83 PDM at 0.24s latency (4.16 Hz, 5.4% of AR latency).
